mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes S 430 or S 580 V8 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M113 engine for the S 430 costs £3,500-£5,000 supply-only; a rebuilt M176 V8 for the S 580 costs £5,200-£8,200 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,500-£2,500 depending on complexity - V8 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil separator failure on a Mercedes S 580?

acceptedAnswer.text: A high-pitched whistling noise at idle, rough idle, or a check engine light are the classic warning signs on the M176 engine. If ignored, it can lead to a blown rear main seal and a massive oil leak.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes S 580 V8 engine (M176) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M176 is a powerful and sophisticated engine, but it has known oil separator issues and CAMTRONIC software vulnerabilities. With these addressed, the engine is proving durable.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes S 430 and S 580 V8 engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M113 engines routinely reach 200,000+ miles. One owner reported an M113 engine exceeding 340,000 miles. The M176 is too new for definitive long-term data, but with proactive maintenance, 100,000+ miles is achievable.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes S 430 or S 580 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the S-Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M113 costs £3,500-£5,000 - comparable to the value of a £3,000-£8,000 vehicle, making it a justifiable investment for well-maintained examples. The S 580's higher value (£45,000-£80,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes S 430 or S 580 V8 need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M113 V8 requires approximately 8.0 litres; the M176 V8 requires approximately 9.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 430/580 V8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The S 430 launched with the W220 generation in 1998 as the entry-level V8 flagship, powered by the M113 4.3-litre naturally aspirated V8 producing 279hp - a robust, SOHC engine that defined Mercedes V8 reliability for over a decade. In 2021, the all-new W223 S 580 introduced the M176 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 with 48V EQ Boost mild-hybrid technology, delivering 496hp and representing a quantum leap in V8 performance and efficiency.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 430/580 V8 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The S 430's M113 V8 and the S 580's M176 V8 represent two very different eras of Mercedes V8 engineering - the M113 is a robust, naturally aspirated SOHC design renowned for durability, while the M176 is a sophisticated twin-turbo DOHC unit with mild-hybrid technology. Both have well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. The M113 suffers from oil leaks and timing chain tensioner wear, while the M176 is prone to oil separator failure and CAMTRONIC software issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M113 Oil Leaks & Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
problems.h4: M113 Oil Leaks & Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - The S 430 V8's Age-Related Issues
problems.rootCause: The M113 V8 is known for developing slow oil leaks over time from valve cover gaskets, oil filter housing gaskets, and the front crankshaft seal. Timing chain tensioner issues can cause rattling noises on startup, and if ignored, can lead to more serious engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gaskets, clean oil seepage
repairOptions.longevity: If oil leaks are minor and localised

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner, inspect chain guides
Complete engine swap with new gaskets, seals, and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil loss or timing failure has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 1998-2006 S 430 is worth approximately £3,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage. These flagship saloons have depreciated significantly, meaning replacement costs can approach vehicle value for higher-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M113 are common with age but not usually urgent unless they are heavy. Valve cover gasket replacement at a specialist is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately - catching it early can prevent more serious engine damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M113 Mercedes S 430 V8 engine prices

problems.h4: M176 Oil Separator (PCV) Failure - The S 580 V8's Most Expensive Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M176 engine suffers from PCV oil separator diaphragm failure. Heat bakes the internal diaphragms of these valves, and a failing separator will often cause a high-pitched whistling noise at idle, a rough idle, or a check engine light, eventually culminating in a blown rear main seal and a massive oil leak. Mercedes-Benz mandates that both oil separators must be replaced anytime a rear main seal is found leaking to prevent repeat failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan, crankcase pressure test, inspect oil separators
repairOptions.longevity: Confirms whether separator or seal is the root cause

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both oil separators (PCV valves), inspect crankcase ventilation system
repairOptions.longevity: If caught before seal damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace rear main seal, drop transmission, inspect flywheel
repairOptions.longevity: If seal has failed but no bottom-end damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded oil separators and rear main seal, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil loss has caused bearing or bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2021-present S 580 is worth approximately £45,000-£80,000 depending on mileage and condition. The S 580 sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value, making a full rebuilt engine a justifiable investment for owners of these high-value V8 flagships.
problems.recommendation: The oil separator is the root cause of most M176 rear main seal leaks. If you hear a whistling noise at idle or notice a rough idle, have the PCV system checked immediately. If caught early, replacing the oil separators alone (£800-£1,400 at a specialist) prevents the much more expensive rear main seal replacement. On an S 580 worth £45,000-£80,000, the full rebuilt engine route is justifiable if bottom-end damage has occurred.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M176 Mercedes S 580 V8 engine prices

problems.group: M176 CAMTRONIC Software & Cylinder Deactivation Issues
problems.h4: M176 CAMTRONIC Software & Cylinder Deactivation Issues - The S 580's Recall Problem
problems.rootCause: A software defect in the engine control unit affects the CAMTRONIC variable valve lift adjustment system. In the event of a mechanical failure in the CAMTRONIC system, the ECU software may cause the engine to overheat or stall. If the CAMTRONIC system fails while the engine is in fuel-saving mode (4 cylinders deactivated), the lambda control system may not deactivate as intended, incorrectly increasing fuel injection, which can raise exhaust gas temperatures and damage components such as the wiring harness or catalytic converter. Over 27,000 vehicles were recalled for this issue.

repairOptions.longevity: Check your VIN for outstanding recall status

problems.recommendation: If your S 580 is subject to the CAMTRONIC recall, have the ECU software update performed at a Mercedes dealer free of charge. If symptoms persist, have the CAMTRONIC system inspected by a specialist. On an S 580 worth £45,000-£80,000, preventative attention to this issue is always the better investment.

problems.rootCause: The M176's twin-turbochargers can suffer from bearing wear due to heat buildup, oil starvation, or actuator malfunctions. The 48V EQ Boost system can also experience battery or ISG (Integrated Starter-Generator) failures, triggering warning lights and loss of hybrid assistance.
